note_on_method: Each venue page rests on two Louisville Parks and Recreation pages: the pickleball page, whose "Pickleball Court List:" gives one line per park with a count and introduces the whole set as outdoor, and the park's own page, which gives a "Park Address", a year acquired, a size in acres, an hours line and an amenity list in which Pickleball is a word without a number. The US Census address geocoder and OpenStreetMap supply the county and the postcode, and because Louisville is a consolidated city-county they name the city three ways. Where the City is silent, on lighting, price, surface, nets and parking at every venue, these pages record the silence.

slots.description:
Fourteen outdoor pickleball courts, the largest set in Louisville by a distance, on one line of the City's pickleball page. The next largest count in the city is six, at four parks, so this one venue holds more than a fifth of the sixty-seven courts verified across Louisville. The park's own page lists "Pickleball" among its amenities without a number, so the fourteen rests on the list and the park page confirms that the courts exist.

The park is 283 acres, acquired in 1957, and its amenity list is one of the longest in the city: ballfields, baseball, basketball, cross country, disc golf, a dog run, fishing, golf, grills, a hiking trail, model airplane flying fields, pickleball, picnic shelters, a playground, restrooms, tennis and WiFi. The courts are one feature among many on a large site.
slots.getting_there: 5550 Charlie Vettiner Park Rd, Louisville, KY 40299. The US Census address file holds no record of it, so the address resolves through OpenStreetMap, which matches it at house-number level and names the place Louisville, one of the three names the resolvers use for the consolidated city. The City publishes nothing about parking. Restrooms are on the amenity list, and on 283 acres the address locates the park rather than the courts.
slots.what_to_expect:
Fourteen courts is a rotation that absorbs a crowd, and it makes this the one Louisville venue where turning up alone is a reasonable plan on the count. Whether a rotation actually forms, and when, is not something the City publishes, so that is an inference from the number rather than a fact from the operator.

The park is open 6 a.m. to 11 p.m. on its own page. Those are park hours. Lighting is not stated, price is not stated, surface is not stated and nets are not stated. The courts are outdoor on the City's own sentence introducing the list.

The park was acquired in 1888 and is 725.85 acres, the second largest published venue in Louisville after McNeely Lake. Its amenity list runs from an amphitheatre and archery through disc golf, golf, hiking and horse riding trails to pickleball, restrooms, a sprayground and tennis. Pickleball is one word on that list, without a count; the four is the pickleball page's.

"2300 Hounz Ln." (Hounz Lane Park) is placed in "Lyndon city". Snapshot: data/sources/louisville-county-census.json
